scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9103: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team blames the fabric -- they say "spine_router_0_0 has failed,
swap the spine". Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device or link to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or
anything beyond. The ticket MISDIRECTS to the fabric / a spine, but the fabric
is healthy: the CLOS fabric is redundant and the OTHER leaf (leaf_router_0_1)
still reaches the fabric normally through both spines, which it could not do if
spine_router_0_0 had failed. The symptom is purely the down access link at
pc_0_0's leaf, not a spine/fabric fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES spine_router_0_0: the
spines and fabric still carry the other leaf, so the user's "spine has failed"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that swaps / blames spine_router_0_0 has followed
the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. spine_router_0_0 / the fabric needs no change.

bonus-exonerates-spine: explicitly notes the spines/fabric still carry the other leaf, rejecting the ticket's spine hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
The outage is due to the access-facing interface on leaf_router_0_0 being down, not a spine failure. On pc_0_0, ARP to its default gateway fails (ip neigh shows “10.0.0.1 dev eth0 FAILED”; ping to 10.0.0.1 returns “Destination Host Unreachable”), which explains why it cannot reach anything off-subnet. Inspecting leaf_router_0_0 shows the customer-facing interface eth2 (the link to pc_0_0) is down: “ip link show dev eth2” reports state DOWN and ethtool reports “Link detected: no.” This prevents ARP replies from 10.0.0.1 and isolates pc_0_0 from the fabric.

Meanwhile, the fabric is healthy: BGP on leaf_router_0_0 is up to both spines (neighbors 172.16.0.4 and 172.16.0.8 in Established with prefixes exchanged), and the leaf has a BGP route to 10.0.1.0/24. This rules out spine_router_0_0 as the culprit.

Localization: leaf_router_0_0, interface eth2 (to pc_0_0). Mechanism: with eth2 down, L2 fails, ARP to the default gateway fails, so the host reports immediate unreachable for any off-link traffic. Root cause: the leaf’s access port is administratively or physically down. Corrective fix: bring the interface back up or reseat the link. Recommended action: on leaf_router_0_0, enable the port (e.g., “ip link set dev eth2 up” or restart the interface/network service) and verify link (ethtool shows Link detected: yes) and that pc_0_0 can resolve 10.0.0.1 via ARP. No spine swap is needed.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names leaf_router_0_0 eth2 as DOWN (ethtool/link state) and exonerates the spine by showing the fabric/BGP is healthy.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states the fabric is healthy (BGP to both spines established and routes present) and explicitly rules out spine_router_0_0 as the culprit.
Proposes bringing eth2 on leaf_router_0_0 back up (e.g., ip link set dev eth2 up), which matches the expected fix.

The investigator demonstrated direct, observed evidence that pc_0_0 is isolated by the leaf's access interface being down (ip link shows eth2 state DOWN; host pings to gateway return 'Destination Host Unreachable'; host RX packets zero), and used that to conclude the leaf access link is the fault and not a spine failure. The writeup's exoneration of the spine is reasonable though the BGP/fabric evidence in the log is somewhat truncated.
